title: Utility Service Maintenance Log Form
subtitle: An original utility service workflow that carries planned or condition-based maintenance through safe release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete utility service maintenance log form for the electric, gas, water, or thermal utility service point that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when service personnel need one record for maintenance trigger, asset baseline, work-control references, recurring events, readings, deferred defects, and qualified return-to-service approval. The utility service coordinator owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Utility service maintenance log identity and ownership
sections.guidance: Define the maintained system, service interval, operating owner, and review period.

sections.title: Utility service asset baseline and maintenance readiness
sections.guidance: Reconcile the exact asset and known condition before maintenance or testing begins.

blocks.label: Planned maintenance task set
items: Verify account, premise, commodity, meter, and service-point identity
Confirm scope ownership between utility and customer equipment
Coordinate interruption, dispatch, traffic, access, and customer notices
Establish site-specific energy, pressure, flow, and public controls
Inspect or service only the authorized utility asset and connection
Record as-found condition, service values, and device status
Complete approved repair, replacement, adjustment, or connection work
Perform authorized leak, electrical, pressure, flow, or functional verification
Record as-left configuration, seals, labels, readings, and photos
Restore service through operations control and confirm customer handoff

sections.title: Utility service work control and safe service boundary
sections.guidance: Record the qualified roles and controlling references; do not use this log as the controlling procedure.

blocks.label: Service readiness confirmations
items: Current procedure, manufacturer information, and applicable requirements were reviewed
Asset boundaries, every energy source, and affected systems were identified
Authorized, affected, contractor, and operations roles were coordinated
Isolation, stored-energy control, and verification references are complete
Required tools, instruments, parts, and protective controls are available
Test, temporary energization, and return-to-service steps have explicit authority
Customer, public, traffic, environmental, and critical-service impacts are controlled
Stop conditions and emergency escalation path are understood

blocks.label: Maintenance stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not use this record to approach downed conductors, investigate a gas odor, enter flooded electrical areas, operate unknown valves or switches, or bypass dispatch control. Keep people clear, use the organization's emergency route, and allow only qualified and authorized personnel to isolate, test, repair, and restore the affected utility service. Maintenance stays restricted when isolation, stored energy, system condition, or work scope is unknown. Only the designated authorized person may direct changes to controls and the qualified release owner may approve return to service.

sections.title: Utility service maintenance events, condition, and readings
sections.guidance: Create a traceable history of work completed, condition found, evidence, and deferred action.

fields.label: Wear pattern, recurring fault, consumable trend, configuration change, and supporting evidence

sections.title: Utility service exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Gas odor, hissing, suspected leak, or atmosphere concern
Downed conductor, arcing, exposed electrical part, or burn damage
Major water release, flooding, washout, or energized equipment in water
Steam, pressure, hot surface, rotating equipment, or uncontrolled stored energy
Traffic, excavation, unstable surface, animal, or uncontrolled public exposure
Unknown valve, switch, disconnect, cross-connection, or service ownership
Critical-load impact or service interruption without operations authorization
Condition requiring emergency dispatch or work beyond assigned qualification
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not use this record to approach downed conductors, investigate a gas odor, enter flooded electrical areas, operate unknown valves or switches, or bypass dispatch control. Keep people clear, use the organization's emergency route, and allow only qualified and authorized personnel to isolate, test, repair, and restore the affected utility service.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each maintenance exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Utility service decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Electric, gas, water, or thermal utility service point identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
